title: A heavier particle in a box
hook: Change particle mass and predict energy eigenvalue.
misconception: energy eigenvalue doubles when particle mass doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) to compare energy eigenvalue when particle mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a particle in a one-dimensional infinite square well with fixed width and quantum number, E_n = n²h²/(8mL²). When particle mass doubles, energy eigenvalue becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model E_n = n²h²/(8mL²); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a particle in a one-dimensional infinite square well with fixed width and quantum number, with a nonzero initial result. If particle mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on energy eigenvalue?
recall.why: Apply E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
